title: The Complexity of Oracle-Efficient Realizable Transductive Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.28757v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In realizable transductive online learning, the learner knows the entire sequence of $T$ instances in advance, and the labels are consistent with one of $N$ hypotheses. With explicit access to the hypothesis class, the halving algorithm makes at most $\log_2 N$ mistakes. Can a comparable guarantee be achieved using only polynomially many empirical risk minimization (ERM) queries? We answer this question negatively, even for a weighted-ERM oracle that optimizes arbitrary real-valued linear objectives and returns a complete maximizing hypothesis. For every fixed $\beta\in(0,1)$ and every randomized learner making polynomially many oracle queries, there exists a fixed realizable instance with exactly $N=2^{\lfloor T^\beta\rfloor}$ hypotheses on which the learner makes $\Omega_\beta(\sqrt{T\log N})$ mistakes in expectation. This matches the agnostic-rate upper bound achieved by random playout using $O(T)$ oracle calls. The separation persist

translated_title: 预言机高效的可实现转换式学习的复杂度
translated_abstract: 在可实现的转换式在线学习中，学习器预先知道整个长度为 $T$ 的实例序列，且标签与 $N$ 个假设中的某一个保持一致。在可以显式访问假设类的情况下，减半算法最多只会犯 $\log_2 N$ 次错误。那么，仅通过多项式次数的经验风险最小化（ERM）查询能否获得可比的保证？我们对这一问题给出了否定回答，即使是针对加权 ERM 预言机——它能够优化任意实值线性目标并返回一个完整的最大化假设——情况也是如此。对于任意固定的 $\beta\in(0,1)$ 以及任何只进行多项式次预言机查询的随机学习器，都存在一个固定的可实现实例，该实例恰好含有 $N=2^{\lfloor T^\beta\rfloor}$ 个假设，在该实例上学习器期望犯 $\Omega_\beta(\sqrt{T\log N})$ 次错误。这一下界与通过 $O(T)$ 次预言机调用进行随机演练所达到的不可知率上界相匹配。这种分离持续存在……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文证明即使借助能优化任意线性目标的加权 ERM 预言机，可实现转换式在线学习也无法通过多项式次预言机查询达到减半算法的对数级错误保证，并给出了与不可知率上界匹配的 $\Omega_\beta(\sqrt{T\log N})$ 期望错误下界。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that even with a weighted-ERM oracle optimizing arbitrary linear objectives, realizable transductive online learning cannot achieve the halving algorithm's logarithmic mistake guarantee with only polynomially many oracle queries, establishing an $\Omega_\beta(\sqrt{T\log N})$ expected mistake lower bound that matches the agnostic-rate upper bound.
